title: backlog.py resume ID sends a follow-up to an item's worker by the session id its dispatch recorded
goal: Retrospective of SP-sbdy4hsx: the orchestrator sent ST-nkr6cpvs's rework with claude -p --resume and a session id typed by hand, which was wrong (No conversation found), and had to start it again. backlog.py resume ID FILE reads the session id from the result dispatch wrote in the item's scratch directory and runs the same claude -p argv in the worker's worktree with FILE on stdin, writing a numbered result beside the first; the kb-sprint skill's run step 4.1 names it; a test runs it with a stubbed claude on a planted scratch directory and finds the recorded id in the argv.

run:
import subprocess,tempfile,os,shutil,re,sys,json
from pathlib import Path
R=os.getcwd(); T=tempfile.mkdtemp()
def sh(*a,env=None): return subprocess.run(a,cwd=T,capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)
sh('git','init','-q','.'); sh('git','-c','user.email=a@b','-c','user.name=n','commit','-q','--allow-empty','-m','init')
shutil.copy(R+'/backlog.json',T); os.makedirs(T+'/kb/_self/backlog')
bl=lambda *a,env=None: sh('python3',R+'/_tools/backlog.py','--root',T,*a,env=env)
iid=re.search(r'ST-\w+',bl('new','story','--title','Resume me','--goal','g').stdout).group(0)
d=bl('dispatch',iid,'--dry-run').stdout
wt=re.search(r'^worktree: (\S+)',d,re.M).group(1); scratch=re.search(r'^scratch: (\S+)',d,re.M).group(1)
top=os.path.realpath(T)
if not (os.path.realpath(wt).startswith(top) and os.path.realpath(scratch).startswith(top)): sys.exit(2)
os.makedirs(wt); os.makedirs(scratch)
Path(scratch,'result.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(session_id='sess-planted-42')))
bd=Path(T,'bin'); bd.mkdir(); log=Path(T,'argv.json'); fake=bd/'claude'
fake.write_text('#!'+sys.executable+'\nimport sys,json,os\njson.dump(dict(argv=sys.argv[1:],stdin=sys.stdin.read(),cwd=os.getcwd()),open('+repr(str(log))+',"w"))\nprint(json.dumps(dict(session_id="sess-planted-42",result="ok")))\n')
fake.chmod(0o755)
msg=Path(T,'followup.md'); msg.write_text('REWORK PLEASE')
env=dict(os.environ,PATH=str(bd)+os.pathsep+os.environ['PATH'])
r=bl('resume',iid,str(msg),env=env)
rec=json.loads(log.read_text()) if log.exists() else dict()
a=rec.get('argv',[])
ok=(r.returncode==0 and '--resume' in a and a[a.index('--resume')+1:][:1]==['sess-planted-42'] and rec.get('stdin')=='REWORK PLEASE'
    and os.path.realpath(rec.get('cwd',''))==os.path.realpath(wt) and len(list(Path(scratch).glob('result*.json')))>=2)
print('resume exit',r.returncode,'argv',a,(r.stderr or '')[-150:])
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

notes: Merged from ST-tuc2zmio “A host orchestrator can resume a returned worker without a cd its permission rules refuse (second-project run)” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: Same need as ST-zpcvcyqs: a backlog.py command that runs claude -p --resume in the worker's worktree, instead of a hand cd and a hand-typed session id. Absorb that the command needs no shell cd, so a host's allow rules accept it, and that the plugin skill names it. Its goal: The plugin's sprint skill gives a way to resume a worker's headless session in its worktree that a host's permission rules allow (a backlog.py command that runs claude -p --resume in the worktree, or a documented allow rule) Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "_tools/tests.py", "-k", "plugin_sprint_resume_worker"]}
